toolCalls.name: StructuredOutput

output.brief:
The slowdown is almost entirely in property-secured loans, and almost entirely in one stage: collateral valuation. That stage went from about 1.6 days in March to 8.4 in August. Unsecured loans are back to about 5.9 days, close to March's 5.6. Since 1 May, the revised credit policy (clause 6.3) has required a full inspection appraisal for exposures between $150k and $500k. Before that, desktop valuations covered this band. Full appraisals take the valuation firm about 8.6 days, against about 1.2 for desktop ones. The firm's turnaround for each type hasn't changed. Full appraisals rose from about 30 a month to about 80. The policy change was never assessed for its effect on processing times.

The evidence does not support the new-hire explanation. Document collection at the hire branches matches the other branches. It also doesn't support blaming the Corvane system: consumer loans and unsecured SME loans are fine. Credit Hub capacity isn't the cause either, because underwriting time is flat. Don't withhold the Corvane payment or put the new hires on improvement plans.

Next step: take the measured delay to the credit risk committee, alongside the audit finding that justified the clause (desktop valuations ran a median 12% above later full appraisals). Ask them to decide whether to keep, narrow or speed up the clause. Add a by-stage breakdown to the dashboard. Whether the longer waits are what's driving withdrawals is still unproven. The auto-close rule may also be inflating the withdrawal figures.
